segments.heading: Every app reads text one character at a time.
segments.sub: A name. A date. A symbol. How does code grab just the piece it needs?
segments.narration: Every app you use is quietly reading text, one character at a time. The first letter of your name. The year inside a date. A single symbol in a password. So how does a program reach in and grab just the piece it needs?

segments.caption: Reach straight to position 0 for her initial.
segments.narration: Say a user signs up as Alice. The app wants just her initial for a profile badge. It doesn't read the whole name. It reaches straight to position zero and pulls out the single letter A.

segments.caption: Slice out the first four characters.
segments.narration: Or take a date typed as 2026-06-09. To show only the year, the program slices out the first four characters. No guessing, no scanning the rest. Just the slice it asked for.

segments.caption: Count backward from the end and land exactly on it.
segments.narration: Even a chat app does this. To grab the last character of a message, maybe to check for a question mark, it counts backward from the end and lands exactly on it.

segments.heading: This is string indexing.
segments.sub: Every character lives at a numbered position. Name the positions, take what you want.
segments.narration: This is string indexing. Every character in a string lives at a numbered position, and you can pull out any one of them, or a range, just by naming the positions you want.

segments.heading: Parsing, cleaning, validating — it all starts here.
segments.sub: Let's learn how to reach into a string and take exactly what you need.
segments.narration: It's one of the most-used skills in all of Python. Parsing files, cleaning data, validating input. It all starts here. So let's learn how to reach into a string and take exactly what you need.
